steps.user_message: I want to file my 2024 taxes correctly. I'm single in Atlanta GA. W-2 from Pacific Software: $68,200. Additional income: $16,300 (photography, 5 clients), $2,100 from Capital One 360, $670 from Schwab. Home office: 120 sq ft exclusive; I pay $1,750/month for 740 sq ft. Deductions: $5,100 student loan interest (Nelnet, 2019–2021); $1,500 to Salvation Army have the receipt; $1,050 unreimbursed expenses. Can you tell me what I can deduct, whether to itemize or take the standard deduction, how to treat the home office, and what forms I need?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with tax-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can walk through this. I’ll summarize what’s deductible, how to treat the home office, whether to itemize vs. take the standard deduction, the forms you’ll use, and next steps/questions so I can give a precise recommendation.

Quick summary
- Report W-2 wages ($68,200) on Form 1040.
- Report photography income ($16,300) on Schedule C (self-employment). That income is subject to income tax and self-employment (SE) tax; you can deduct half of SE tax as an adjustment to income.
- Report interest income (Capital One + Schwab = $2,770) on Form 1040 (and use Schedule B if total interest/dividends > $1,500).
- Home office (120 sq ft exclusive, 740 sq ft home, rent $1,750/mo) is allowed for your self‑employment if used regularly and exclusively for the photography business. You can choose simplified or actual method — see calculations below.
- Charitable gift ($1,500 to Salvation Army) is deductible only if you itemize.
- Student loan interest: only interest paid in the tax year is potentially deductible (max $2,500, phased out by income). I need to know how much interest you actually paid in 2024 and whether you have Form 1098‑E.
- Unreimbursed employee expenses (the $1,050) generally are NOT deductible for most taxpayers since the TCJA (unless you’re in a very narrow category of employees). If those were business expenses related to your photography work (not employee unreimbursed expenses), they would belong on Schedule C.

Home office — two methods (quick comparisons)
- Simplified method: $5.00 × 120 sq ft = $600 deduction for the year.
- Actual method: allocate rent and other home expenses by business percentage = 120/740 ≈ 16.22%. On rent: $1,750 × 12 = $21,000; 21,000 × 16.22% ≈ $3,405. If you have utilities, renter’s insurance, repairs, etc., a portion of those can also be allocated — that typically makes the actual method more valuable in your case (since rent portion alone > simplified deduction).
- If you use the actual method you generally complete Form 8829 (Expenses for Business Use of Your Home) and carry the result to Schedule C. If you use simplified, you just enter the simplified home office deduction on Schedule C and do not file Form 8829.

Itemize vs standard deduction
- To decide, add up deductible itemized amounts: charitable ($1,500) + state/local taxes paid (Georgia income tax and any property tax — note SALT cap of $10,000) + mortgage interest (if any) + other allowable itemized deductions.
- If the sum of itemized deductions is greater than the standard deduction for the tax year, itemize; otherwise take the standard deduction.
- Note: the home office deduction is a business expense on Schedule C — it reduces your net business income (and thus AGI), but it does NOT go on Schedule A as an itemized deduction. So the home office deduction can make the standard deduction relatively more attractive by lowering AGI while itemized deductions remain modest.
- Based on the numbers you gave (charity $1,500; no mortgage interest shown; no SALT amount provided), it’s likely the standard deduction will be larger than your itemized total — but confirm state and property taxes or other itemizable amounts before deciding.

Student loan interest deduction
- Only interest paid in the filing year qualifies (up to $2,500, with MAGI phaseouts). If your $5,100 is total paid over several years (2019–2021) it does not mean you can deduct $5,100 for a later year. Check Form 1098‑E from Nelnet for the tax year to see the exact eligible amount. If you have eligibility, the deduction is an adjustment on Schedule 1 (reduces AGI).

Unreimbursed employee expenses
- Typically not deductible for employees (suspended under TCJA) — if these $1,050 are actually business expenses for your photography business, put them on Schedule C instead.

Forms you will likely use
- Form 1040 (U.S. Individual Income Tax Return)
- Schedule 1 (Additional Income and Adjustments) — for adjustments like half of SE tax, student loan interest (if eligible), etc.
- Schedule C (Profit or Loss from Business) — to report photography income and business expenses, and to claim home office deduction (either via Schedule C line for simplified or via Form 8829 if using actual).
- Schedule SE (Self-Employment Tax) — to compute SE tax on your net self-employment income.
- Form 8829 — if you use the actual expense method for home office.
- Schedule B — if your combined interest/dividend income exceeds $1,500 (you have $2,770 total, so schedule B applies).
- Form 1099‑NEC/1099‑K/1099‑INT — keep these for records (you’ll receive 1099s if applicable).
- State return: Georgia individual return (check GA form requirements — you will file a GA return and report the same incomes subject to Georgia rules).

Other tax items to watch
- Self-employment tax: roughly 15.3% on net SE income (you also subtract half of SE tax as an adjustment). Net SE income = gross self-employment receipts minus allowable business expenses (including home office).
- Quarterly estimated tax payments: because of self‑employment income you may need to make (or have made) estimated tax payments during the year to avoid penalties. Use Form 1040‑ES worksheets to compute.
- Keep receipts/invoices for business expenses and the charity receipt you mentioned.

What I need from you to be more specific / next steps
1. Confirm whether the $5,100 student loan interest was paid in 2024 (or provide the amount paid in 2024 and/or 1098‑E).
2. Confirm whether the $1,050 unreimbursed expenses are business expenses for photography (receipts) or employee unreimbursed expenses.
3. Tell me any state income tax or property tax amounts you paid in 2024 (SALT) and whether you have mortgage interest (Form 1098).
4. Do you want me to: a) estimate taxable income and rough tax/SE tax numbers, b) draft an email summarizing these details to a CPA, or c) prepare a checklist/worksheet you can use to file?

If you want, I can draft an email to a tax preparer with the information above (or prepare a concise summary/checklist) — tell me which and provide the recipient address and any extra instructions.
